messages:
Alex: Quick sync — packing this thread so we don't lose context. Customer Y asked for per-tenant 'pinned capacity' for Dedicated. They want guaranteed high-priority lanes during business hours and the ability to buy extra 'capacity reservation tokens' that carry some hours each month. Proposal: sell tokens that map to reserved vGPU-hours with priority routing + soft carryover. Need alignment on scope, pricing, ops, and contract language.

Jamie: They told me they'll sign a 12mo if we can do 3 tokens with daily carryover and a 99.95% priority-window SLA. Willing to pay a premium.

Ravi: Engineering reality check — physically pinning GPUs per-tenant is a hard isolation promise. Alternative is virtual "priority lanes": task weighting + admission control + preemption for low-priority jobs. That gives the customer observed preferential latency but not hard physical isolation. Requires new quota/accounting and routing tag.

Sam: Platform note — we can prototype soft-reservation: allocate a fixed pool of capacity for tokens, but allow pre-emption rules. Ops needs a metric for token utilization and blocked requests. Rough ETA for an alpha: ~6 weeks if prioritized.

Mei: High level pricing POV — price per token should reflect the expected reserved-hours + risk buffer for unused capacity. Quick rule: monthly_token_price = cost_reserved_hours * 1.6 + SLA_credit_provision. Also recommend a minimum term (3mo) to make capacity planning feasible. I'll run numbers and post a tile.

Nora: From CS — customers care about burst behavior during launches. If we only offer soft-reservation, customers still accept it if fallback is clearly documented (e.g., guaranteed priority for X hours/day, then fallback to best-effort). Rollover is important to them — 'use-or-lose' is a dealbreaker.

LegalBot: Contract constraints — we cannot promise "pinned physical nodes" unless the customer buys a dedicated isolated cluster (Private/Dedicated with per-tenant hardware). Suggested language: "Customer will receive priority routing and reserved capacity subject to operational constraints; in the event of material shortfall Redwood will provide service credits as defined in SLA." No hard-isolation promises without a dedicated cluster add-on.

Alex: Draft launch criteria I'm proposing: 1) implement soft-reservation token alpha with telemetry (per-token latency distribution, utilization), 2) 3 pilot customers signed up, 3) fallback behavior documented and ops/playbook in place, 4) legal-approved contract language with clear SLA/credits. MVE = soft-reservation tokens (no physical pinning). Approve? :eyes:

Jamie: +1 from sales — will push Customer Y and another pilot to test 3 tokens each for 3 months. We'll accept the soft guarantee if credits/rollover are clarified. :thumbsup:

Ravi: I'll start a design doc (will link here when ready) and include the admission control algorithm, metrics to emit, and an ops runbook for pre-emption. Sample policy draft: 
```
policy:
  token_id: TKN-001
  reserved_hours_per_month: 120
  priority_weight: 80
  rollover: true
```

Sam: Ops checklist: telemetry + tagging, quota accounting, routable tag in request headers, and a dashboard. Also need a backstop circuit to prevent token usage from starving system processes.

Mei: I'll produce a pricing tile and 'what-if' calculator (cost vs. utilization scenarios) and add a recommended list price with a 30% pilot discount.

LegalBot: I'll draft fallback SLA text and standardize credit calculations. Also note we should not tie availability to specific hardware unless customer signs for Dedicated private cluster.

Alex: Action items: Ravi - design doc + runbook; Sam - telemetry & ops checklist; Mei - pricing tile & calculator; LegalBot - contract fallback language; Nora - coordinate pilot customers. Revisit in 2 weeks (Thursday sync). Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
